title: PulseGrid: token-latency differential visualization for per-route/model dashboards
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Design an interactive canvas (PulseGrid) for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-route and per-model token-level latency differences and throughput trends. The canvas should help engineers and product owners quickly identify latency regressions tied to model versions, input token prefixes, and regional routing. It will live on the route and model detail pages as a primary performance panel.

Core ideas: differential sparklines (compare baseline vs current), token-latency heat lanes, throughput ribbon, outlier swimlane for tail latency, and an adaptive bucketing algorithm that summarizes long traces without losing token-local spikes. The design must specify chart layers, interaction affordances, color semantics, and accessibility considerations.
acceptance_criteria: PulseGrid prototype available in Figma with 3 breakpoints (desktop/tablet/mobile)
Design spec includes: data schema for charts, recommended rollup functions, bucket sizing rules, tooltip content and copy
Handoff doc lists API fields required from the runtime team and example payloads (start/end, tokens[], latencies[], model_version)
Accessibility: color contrast verified, keyboard drill-in to swimlane rows, screen-reader-friendly summary text provided
UX review feedback incorporated and signoff from PM and Eng leads
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Patel: Added initial problem statement and wireframes. Calling out need for a differential mode to compare baseline (last deployed stable) vs current traffic.
2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Iterated interaction where users can drag-select a token range to re-run evals and pin to the right-hand panel. Need guidance from runtime on payload size limits.
2026-03-11 Diego Ramos (Eng): Noted runtime can provide token-level latencies for sampled traces; suggested server-side bucketing for long sequences to reduce payloads.
2026-03-12 Priya Singh (PM): Requested a low-fidelity 'compact mode' for side-by-side model comparisons in space-constrained consoles. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 UX Review: Minor copy updates and adjust legend behavior when multiple model versions are visible.
tradeoffs: Client-side bucketing preserves interactivity but may overload browsers for million-token traces
Server-side bucketing reduces client cost but hides some token-local spikes unless an adaptive sampler is used
Showing token-level detail for every trace is high-bandwidth; choose sampling + on-demand expansion
spec_highlights: Token-latency Heat Lanes: horizontal lanes per percentile band (p50/p90/p99) with per-token color intensity tied to latency delta against baseline
Differential Sparklines: micro-sparklines that overlay baseline vs current; tappable to promote to full timeline
Throughput Ribbon: compact stacked area showing requests/sec by model version or route variant
Outlier Swimlane: rows that show traces with top tail latency events; clicking a row opens trace-level waterfall
Adaptive Bucketing: rules and pseudocode included in handoff doc; default: linear buckets up to 512 tokens, then exponential coarsening
Interactive behaviors: brush-to-zoom, hover tooltip with token text, latency, model_version, request_id; pin-to-panel to lock selection for further operations
Data rollups: explicit functions for aggregation (mean, median, p90/p99, count, sample_count) listed in spec
runtime_api_contract_examples: Response fields: start, end, tokens[], latencies[], model_version, region, trace_id (nullable), aggregated_metrics{p50,p90,p99,throughput}
handoff_notes: Engineering must implement an adaptive sampler that returns a compressed token run-length encoding for long traces
Provide a lightweight 'summary-only' endpoint for initial render and an 'expand' endpoint for token-level details on demand
Include a server-side flag for 'baseline_version' which the console can use to compute deltas if the client cannot afford baseline payloads
ux_considerations: Color semantics: green = within baseline, amber = 1.5x baseline, red = >=2x baseline; include user-overridable thresholds
Small multiples: allow 1..4 lanes to be compared side-by-side (models or routes)
Performance: prefer canvas or WebGL rendering for heat lanes at >1000 tokens
Mobile fallback: show condensed sparklines and a readout of hotspots rather than full heat lanes
accessibility_notes: All interactive controls reachable by keyboard; brush selection via shift+arrow keys
Provide summarized textual description of chart state for screen readers (pre-generated by server when feasible)
Ensure colorblind-friendly palette and pattern overlays for critical states
